correctness.summary: The invariant CDGA calculation checks out. In J^S2, d(e)=p+q, d(s1e)=2r and d(qe)=w, leaving cohomology only in degrees 0,2,4 with generator [s1], nonzero square and zero cube. The maps from (Λ(x_2,y_5),dy=x^3) given by x↦s1,y↦(3/2)s1e and to Q[t]/(t^3) by x↦t,y↦0 are chain maps and quasi-isomorphisms. Because CP^2 is smooth projective, the Kriz/Lambrechts-Stanley model is available over Q, and finite-group invariants are exact in characteristic zero.

limitations: The conclusion is rational/real formality only.
The result concerns two unordered points on CP^2, not a general n-point theorem.
output/artifacts/verify_formality.py is absent from the audited repository tree; the algebra was rechecked directly.
The originality assessment treats the result as an explicit specialization of established configuration-space models.

originality.summary: The model theorem is established literature. The contribution is best understood as an explicit CP^2 specialization and formality zigzag rather than a new general formality theorem. Focused search did not surface the exact unordered two-point computation in the cited sources.

scientific_value.summary: The explicit zigzag cleanly resolves the named formality question and identifies the rational cohomology and minimal model.
